findings.evidence: “Judgment never moves a verdict: grouping, spacing rhythm, type-scale count, the squint test and wording stay out of the table. Mention them after the summary line only when the user asks for polish notes.”
findings.fix: Retain the objective eight-rule checklist, but allow a separate, clearly labeled judgment-based assessment when a diagnostic or polish request calls for it, including when the user does not explicitly say 'polish notes'.

findings.evidence: “Fail: ... a pointer target under 24 by 24 CSS px” conflicts with the spacing, equivalent-control, inline, user-agent and essential exceptions listed in references/rules/a11y.md.
findings.fix: Make the main a11y rule apply the WCAG 2.5.8 exceptions before failing a small target; when the needed spacing or context is unknown, mark the criterion unverified and load references/rules/a11y.md for the exception.

findings.evidence: “not a flex item (the target's root counts as not one)” treats a component root as unable to shrink even when its actual parent is a flex container.
findings.fix: Determine whether the rendered root is a flex item from its parent layout; if the parent is outside the supplied scope, mark shrinkability unverified rather than failing solely on its declared width. Add an eval with a wide component root inside a shrinking flex container.

findings.evidence: “The list skeleton is in the passing example in `SKILL.md`” points to no complete passing list example; SKILL.md contains only a single skeleton fragment.
findings.fix: Provide a complete list-loading example in a reference file and link to it here, or correct this pointer to describe the existing fragment and supply the missing list context.

findings.evidence: “Fix pattern: the passing example in `SKILL.md`” points to fragments rather than a complete example showing the pending, empty, error, retry and success branches.
findings.fix: Add a complete states fix pattern to a reference file and link to it here, or replace the pointer with accurate links to the existing fragments and a complete branch example.

findings.evidence: responsive rule 1 fails any declared min-width over 320 px outside a scroll container, while the invoices eval expects na for invoices.css:3 `min-width: 48rem` inside `.table-scroll { overflow-x: auto }`
findings.fix: In responsive rule 1, exempt a min-width that sits on a table, map or code block inside its own scroll container (the allowance the Rule intro and Trap already give), and fail only a page-level or non-excepted container; keep the invoices eval's na verdict.

findings.evidence: Judgment aids include 'Delete filler copy ("Welcome to your dashboard") and repeated "Overview" headings.'
findings.fix: Move that filler-copy line to the end of references/rules/hierarchy.md under a short examples note, or record the removal in docs/audit/recovery/ui-ux-principles/record.md; the model produces it unprompted and it is not a fail line.

findings.evidence: disabled | Looks inert and is inert | practice, no fetched source
findings.fix: Replace the disabled row's requirement with the sourced inert test already in Decisions (native disabled, or aria-disabled plus a handler that blocks the action) and drop the unsourced 'practice' cell.

findings.evidence: loading.md restates that the wait thresholds, submit rule and decide-by-scope rule live in SKILL.md ## loading
findings.fix: Delete that restating intro and record it in docs/audit/recovery/ui-ux-principles/record.md; the file should open on the decisions that are not already in SKILL.md.

findings.evidence: Render offers Playwright and the harness browser tool as equal options, with no default
findings.fix: Default to the harness browser tool when the session has one, and use Playwright only when it does not.

findings.evidence: review-scrolling-table expects responsive na for invoices.css min-width 48rem inside an overflow container, which responsive rule 1 marks fail
findings.fix: After the rule-1 scroll-container exemption, keep this eval; until then its expected na verdict cannot be produced by following the skill.
